summary.text: ASA is acrylonitrile styrene acrylate. Makers sell it for outdoor and weather-exposed parts, citing its UV resistance. Its HDT at 0.45 MPa is 96 °C, below its glass transition, and across the layers a part keeps about 59 % of its flat tensile strength. On the H2C it prints with a standard nozzle, but Bambu Lab's Filament Guide requires an enclosure, and some products ask for more chamber heat than the H2C reaches.

items.text: Natural color ASA coupons were built on the F900 using the T16 tip with 0.254 mm (0.010 in.) layer height. The coupons were then tested before and after UV exposure. Ten ASTM D638 upright (ZX) coupons were tested in tensile after UV exposure and an additional 10 ASTM D638 ZX coupons were the control (no UV Exposure). The UV exposed samples were cycled in the QUV chamber per ASTM G154 (Standard Practice for Operating Fluorescent Ultraviolet (UV) Lamp Apparatus for Exposure of Non-Metallic Materials) for 1000 hours, alternating for 8 hours at 60 °C (140 °F) and 4 hours at 50 °C (122 °F) with humidity and condensation. The increase in stress in break is from the control samples. For more information see the Impact of UV Exposure on FDM Materials white paper.
